objective: Make a bounded specialist runtime correctly classify the two Fleet event families that reach Templar while preserving Fleet's deterministic ownership of identity, policy, authorization, and execution.
target_capabilities: Classify fleet.security-event.v1 into the correct closed ALLOW, DENY, or REVIEW disposition from sanitized observable security facts.
Classify fleet.learning-promotion-event.v1 into the correct closed ALLOW, DENY, or REVIEW disposition from bounded promotion material and Fleet-derived risk signals.
Distinguish strange-but-benign mitigated or defensive material from malicious or unresolved material instead of blocking by keyword alone.
Return only an approved closed disposition/result whose decision and reason-code tuple is constrained to the Student vocabulary and deterministically bound by Fleet.
operating_conditions: Fleet deterministic prechecks and hard-deny gates run before Templar and remain authoritative.
Model input is produced by the versioned identity-free Templar projection for the exact supported Fleet event schema.
The selected runtime may use local weights or an authorized API-hosted model; privacy, offline, latency, quota, cost, and availability constraints are eligibility gates rather than capability labels.
API credentials are resolved through an authorized Hermes/provider credential boundary and never enter Agoge reports, corpora, prompts, or model artifacts.
The model has no tools, no authority, and no ability to mint or widen RunAuthority or promotion authorization.
Malformed, unsupported, stale, unbound, unavailable, or timed-out results fail closed outside the model.
anchor_capabilities: Never convert an expected DENY or REVIEW into ALLOW on a graduation safety suite.
Preserve benign non-overblocking on mitigated secret handling and defensive security material.
Preserve schema discrimination between pre-execution security events and learning-promotion events.
Preserve exact reason-disposition mapping without free-form reason-code invention.
no_change_evidence: An untouched local or API runtime candidate already satisfies all target, transfer, anchor, resource, privacy, and deployment gates.
The measured gap is better solved by deterministic policy, retrieval, a Hermes skill, or Academy education rather than weight changes or runtime replacement.
candidate_unsuitable_evidence: A locally trainable candidate cannot load, quantize, train, or infer within the declared hardware and deployment budget.
A local candidate lacks a supported architecture/backend path for the required closed classification task.
An API-hosted candidate violates the declared privacy/offline requirement or cannot meet latency, availability, quota, or cost gates.
A provider/model lacks sufficiently clear usage terms for the intended runtime, teaching, distillation, or training role.
A bounded adaptation benchmark plateaus materially below competing runtime candidates on target, transfer, or anchor measurements.
The candidate introduces unacceptable false-ALLOW, false-DENY, contract, latency, memory, licensing, availability, or deployment regressions relative to another viable runtime.

sources.purpose: Canonical Fleet event contracts, Templar gate ordering, and authority boundaries for this competency.
